full_judgment:
Md Rezaul Haque J: This is an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the judgment and order dated 30-11-2014 passed by Ms Mosammat Zakia Parvin, Metropolitan Additional Sessions judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Metro Criminal Revision No. 757 of 2014 rejecting the revision and thereby affirming the Order No. 6, dated 14-8-2014 so far it relates to rejection of application for taking opinion of the hand writing expert, passed by Ms Nur Nahar Begum Shiuly, Joint Metro Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Metro Sessions Case No. 9291 of 2013 arising out of CR Case No. 26 of 2013 under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. 

 2. Short facts are that the opposite-party No. 2, being complainant filed a petition of Complaint against the accused Petitioner under sections 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881. The Court concerned took cognizance against the petitioner and the petitioner obtained bail. Ultimately the case record was communicated to the court of Joint Metropolitan sessions Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, for trial. Charge was framed properly, PW 1 was examined and also was cross examined. On 14-8-2014 the petitioner filed an application before the trial court stating that the signature upon the cheque in question has not been done by the petitioner, so the signature is needed to be examined by the hand writing expert but the learned judge of the trial court dismissed the prayer against which the accused being petitioner filed a revisional application, which was ultimately heard by the learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions judge, 1st Court, Dhaka, but the same was also rejected on 30-11-2014. Thereafter; the petitioner filed this miscellaneous .case under sections 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure challenging the orders of the courts below. 

 4. Mr Md Fazlur Rahman Khan, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the state has opposed the application and has submitted that the petitioner after cross examination of PW 1 has filed this application for obtaining opinion of the hand writing expert with a malafide intention to delay the case as such, the application is liable to be rejected. 

 6. It appears from the record that the petitioner claimed that he did not issue any cheque in favour of the complainant-opposite party No. 2. Though after completion of cross-examination of PW 1, the petitioner has filed an application for taking opinion of hand writing expert, yet, the petitioner should get a chance to prove his defence case. But considering the facts and circumstances of the case we are not eager to issue rule at his stage. In our view demand of Justice would be met if the petitioner is given a chance to obtain the opinion of the hand writing expert as to the genuineness of the Signature upon the cheque in question. Thus, the trial court is directed to send the cheque to the hand writing expert, CID, Dhaka, for obtaining opinion from the said agency within shortest possible time. The CID authority is directed to give their opinion upon the matter within 30 days from the date of receipt of the order from the court Concerned.
